name: security
note: Security / code-review accuracy benchmark (50 tasks). Ground-truth is OWASP/CWE-grounded and checkable: identify-the-vuln and state-the-fix are graded by regex tolerant of valid phrasings but strict enough to reject a wrong class; yes/no safety judgments by exact (prompts demand a bare word); CWE classes by regex with word boundaries (number grader is avoided for CWE because firstNumber('CWE-89') extracts -89). A wrong answer must fail. ~20% held-out.

tasks.prompt: Code review. This builds a query as: query = "SELECT * FROM users WHERE name = '" + username + "'". Name the vulnerability class in one short phrase.
tasks._solution: String-concatenated user input into SQL = SQL injection (CWE-89, OWASP A03). Pattern rejects XSS/other names.

tasks.prompt: Code review. A web app runs: document.getElementById('out').innerHTML = location.hash. Name the vulnerability class.
tasks._solution: Untrusted location.hash written to innerHTML = (DOM-based) cross-site scripting, CWE-79.

tasks.prompt: Code review. A Python handler runs: os.system("ping -c 1 " + user_host). Name the vulnerability class.
tasks._solution: User input concatenated into an OS shell command = OS command injection, CWE-78.

tasks.prompt: Code review. A handler runs: open('/var/data/' + request.args['file']).read() with no validation. Name the vulnerability class.
tasks._solution: Unvalidated filename lets ../ escape the base dir = path/directory traversal, CWE-22.

tasks.prompt: Code review. A server endpoint does: requests.get(request.args['url']) and returns the body to the caller. Name the vulnerability class.
tasks._solution: Server fetches a user-supplied URL = server-side request forgery, CWE-918, OWASP A10.

tasks.prompt: Code review. @app.get('/invoice/<id>') returns db.get_invoice(id) with no check that the invoice belongs to the logged-in user. Name the vulnerability class.
tasks._solution: Object fetched by user-controlled id with no ownership check = IDOR / broken object-level authorization, CWE-639, OWASP A01.

tasks.prompt: Code review. Source contains: AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY = "wJalrXUtnFEMI/K7MDENG/bPxRfiCYEXAMPLEKEY". Name the vulnerability class in one short phrase.
tasks._solution: Secret embedded in source = use of hard-coded credentials, CWE-798.

tasks.prompt: Code review. On signup the app runs: db.save(username, password) storing the password string exactly as received. Name the security problem in one short phrase.
tasks._solution: Passwords stored verbatim = plaintext / unhashed password storage, CWE-256/CWE-312.

tasks.prompt: Code review. @app.get('/admin/all-users') def all_users(): return dump_users() has no authentication or authorization check. Name the vulnerability class.
tasks._solution: Sensitive endpoint with no auth gate = missing authentication / broken access control, CWE-306.

tasks.prompt: Code review. A handler runs: obj = pickle.loads(request.body) on data from the client. Name the vulnerability class.
tasks._solution: Deserializing untrusted data with pickle = insecure deserialization, CWE-502, OWASP A08.

tasks.prompt: Code review. A login handler ends with: return redirect(request.args.get('next')) using the raw value. Name the vulnerability class.
tasks._solution: Redirect target taken unvalidated from user input = open redirect, CWE-601.

tasks.prompt: Code review. A bank app changes state with GET /transfer?to=X&amount=Y and uses no per-request token, so a hostile page can trigger it while the victim is logged in. Name the vulnerability class.
tasks._solution: State-changing request with no anti-forgery token = cross-site request forgery, CWE-352.

tasks.prompt: Code review. Passwords are hashed with hashlib.md5(password.encode()).hexdigest() and no salt. Name the weakness in one short phrase.
tasks._solution: MD5 unsalted for passwords = use of a weak/fast/broken hash unsuitable for passwords, CWE-327/CWE-916.

tasks.prompt: Code review. An XML parser is configured to resolve external entities (DTDs enabled) on documents uploaded by users. Name the vulnerability class (its common acronym is fine).
tasks._solution: External-entity resolution on untrusted XML = XML external entity injection (XXE), CWE-611.

tasks.prompt: Code review. A session token is generated with: token = str(random.random()). Name the security problem in one short phrase.
tasks._solution: random.random() is a non-cryptographic PRNG = insecure/predictable randomness, CWE-330/CWE-338.

tasks.prompt: Code review. A calculator endpoint runs: result = eval(request.args['expr']) on the raw user string. Name the vulnerability class.
tasks._solution: eval() on untrusted input = code injection / arbitrary code execution, CWE-94/CWE-95.

tasks.prompt: Code review. On login failure the app writes: log.info('login failed for ' + username + ' pw=' + password). Name the security problem in one short phrase.
tasks._solution: Logging the plaintext password = sensitive data exposure via logs, CWE-532/CWE-200.

tasks.prompt: Code review. The app never sets X-Frame-Options or a frame-ancestors CSP, so any site can embed its pages in a hidden iframe over a decoy. Name the attack this enables.
tasks._solution: Framing with no frame-busting header = clickjacking (UI redressing), CWE-1021.

tasks.prompt: Code review. A user-update handler runs: user.update(**request.json) binding every JSON field directly to the model, including is_admin. Name the vulnerability class.
tasks._solution: Binding all client fields to the model = mass assignment / over-posting, CWE-915.

tasks.prompt: Code review. An HTTPS client call is made as: requests.get(url, verify=False). Name the security problem in one short phrase.
tasks._solution: verify=False disables TLS certificate validation, enabling MITM, CWE-295.

tasks.prompt: A SQL query is built by concatenating a user-supplied name into the WHERE clause. State the correct fix in one short phrase.
tasks._solution: Canonical SQLi fix = parameterized queries / prepared statements with bound parameters. Rejects 'escaping only'.

tasks.prompt: User-controlled text is inserted into an HTML page and executes as script. State the correct fix for this XSS in one short phrase.
tasks._solution: XSS fix = contextual output encoding / escaping (or sanitization / textContent / CSP), OWASP XSS Prevention.

tasks.prompt: An API key is hard-coded in source. State where the secret should live instead, in one short phrase.
tasks._solution: Fix for hard-coded secret = environment variable / secrets manager / vault, not source.

tasks.prompt: Name an appropriate algorithm (or family) for securely hashing user passwords.
tasks._solution: OWASP Password Storage: bcrypt, argon2, scrypt, or PBKDF2. Rejects md5/sha.

tasks.prompt: A server fetches a user-supplied URL (SSRF risk). State the correct mitigation in one short phrase.
tasks._solution: SSRF fix = allowlist destinations + block internal/metadata ranges, OWASP SSRF Prevention.

tasks.prompt: An endpoint returns a record by id without checking it belongs to the caller (IDOR). State the correct fix in one short phrase.
tasks._solution: IDOR fix = enforce authorization / ownership (object-level access control) on every access.

tasks.prompt: A state-changing form has no protection against cross-site request forgery. State the correct defense in one short phrase.
tasks._solution: CSRF fix = anti-CSRF (synchronizer) token and/or SameSite cookies, OWASP CSRF Prevention.

tasks.prompt: A program runs a shell command built from user input. State the correct fix to prevent command injection, in one short phrase.
tasks._solution: Command-injection fix = avoid the shell; pass an argument array (shell=False / execve) or allowlist, OWASP.

tasks.prompt: A file is opened from a path that includes a user-supplied name (path traversal risk). State the correct mitigation in one short phrase.
tasks._solution: Path-traversal fix = canonicalize/resolve the path and confirm it stays within the allowed base dir, CWE-22 remediation.

tasks.prompt: Login credentials are sent over plain HTTP. State the correct fix in one short phrase.
tasks._solution: Plaintext transport fix = use TLS / HTTPS to encrypt in transit, CWE-319 remediation.

tasks.prompt: An app deserializes untrusted data with a native binary deserializer (e.g. pickle). State the correct fix in one short phrase.
tasks._solution: Insecure-deserialization fix = don't deserialize untrusted data with native formats; use JSON/data-only formats, or signed+allowlisted types, CWE-502 remediation.

tasks.prompt: Is storing user passwords in plaintext a safe practice? Answer with only one word, yes or no.
tasks._solution: Plaintext password storage is never safe (CWE-256). Answer: no.

tasks.prompt: Is MD5 an appropriate algorithm for hashing user passwords? Answer with only one word, yes or no.
tasks._solution: MD5 is fast and broken; unsuitable for password hashing (OWASP). Answer: no.

tasks.prompt: Is it safe to pass untrusted user input directly to eval()? Answer with only one word, yes or no.
tasks._solution: eval() on untrusted input = code injection (CWE-95). Answer: no.

tasks.prompt: Is bcrypt an appropriate choice for hashing user passwords? Answer with only one word, yes or no.
tasks._solution: bcrypt is an OWASP-recommended adaptive password hash. Answer: yes.

tasks.prompt: Are parameterized queries (prepared statements) an effective defense against SQL injection? Answer with only one word, yes or no.
tasks._solution: Parameterized queries are the primary, effective SQLi defense (OWASP). Answer: yes.

tasks.prompt: In production, is it safe to disable TLS certificate validation (e.g. verify=False)? Answer with only one word, yes or no.
tasks._solution: Disabling cert validation enables MITM (CWE-295). Answer: no.

tasks.prompt: Is TLS 1.0 considered secure by modern standards? Answer with only one word, yes or no.
tasks._solution: TLS 1.0 is deprecated (RFC 8996); not secure. Answer: no.

tasks.prompt: Should secrets such as API keys and passwords be committed into a git repository? Answer with only one word, yes or no.
tasks._solution: Committing secrets to VCS = hard-coded/exposed credentials (CWE-798). Answer: no.

tasks.prompt: Give the CWE identifier for SQL injection (format: CWE-NN).
tasks._solution: SQL injection = CWE-89. Boundary rejects CWE-79/CWE-890.

tasks.prompt: Give the CWE identifier for cross-site scripting (format: CWE-NN).
tasks._solution: XSS = CWE-79. Boundary rejects CWE-89/CWE-798.

tasks.prompt: Give the CWE identifier for path traversal (format: CWE-NN).
tasks._solution: Path traversal = CWE-22. Boundary rejects CWE-222.

tasks.prompt: Give the CWE identifier for OS command injection (format: CWE-NN).
tasks._solution: OS command injection = CWE-78. Boundary rejects CWE-789/CWE-787.

tasks.prompt: Give the CWE identifier for cross-site request forgery (format: CWE-NNN).
tasks._solution: CSRF = CWE-352.

tasks.prompt: Give the CWE identifier for server-side request forgery (format: CWE-NNN).
tasks._solution: SSRF = CWE-918.

tasks.prompt: Give the CWE identifier for use of hard-coded credentials (format: CWE-NNN).
tasks._solution: Hard-coded credentials = CWE-798.

tasks.prompt: Give the CWE identifier for deserialization of untrusted data (format: CWE-NNN).
tasks._solution: Insecure deserialization = CWE-502.

tasks.prompt: Give the CWE identifier for open redirect / URL redirection to untrusted site (format: CWE-NNN).
tasks._solution: Open redirect = CWE-601.

tasks.prompt: Name the lowest version of TLS that is still considered secure (not deprecated) today. Give the version number.
tasks._solution: TLS 1.0/1.1 deprecated (RFC 8996); lowest still-secure version is TLS 1.2. Rejects 1.0/1.1/3.0.

tasks.prompt: Name a widely deployed hash algorithm that is now considered cryptographically broken for collision resistance and should not be used for new security work. (One example is enough.)
tasks._solution: MD5 and SHA-1 are broken for collision resistance (NIST). Rejects sha-256/sha-512.
